Figure 1:Overview of WorldExam.WorldExam is a hierarchical diagnostic benchmark fromapparent appearancetoinherent reactivity.
It evaluates 1,474 test cases across camera-, action-, and language-driven interfaces, four diagnostic levels, and eight tasks under a unified evaluation pipeline.

Figure 2:WorldExam taxonomy, tracks, and metrics.Four diagnostic levels map to eight evaluation tasks, which are assigned to static-scene or dynamic-interaction tracks according to scene assumptions and model applicability.
Each track reports task-specific and general metrics.
Representative examples illustrate the geometry-based evaluations.

Figure 3:Test case curation pipeline.For the six dynamic-interaction tasks, a task pattern is expanded into a structured draft, candidate initial images are generated and human-filtered, and the scene description, text prompt, and optional checklist are refined against the selected image before the case is finalized.

Figure 5:Image-space displacement alignment for camera-driven models.Given an initial image and anchor mask for casecc, WorldExam measures modelmm’s image-space displacementdm,cd_{m,c}in a default-input calibration pass and scales its input translations bykm,c=W/(2​dm,c)k_{m,c}=W/(2d_{m,c})to align displacement across camera-driven models.

Figure 6:Geometry-based evaluation of Subject Control and Terrain Interaction.(a) SAM2 and VGGT-Ω\Omegarecover the subject trajectory, while the horizontal-region mask estimates gravity and the horizontal plane used to define the control directions.
(b) A subject-free image restores the complete terrain geometry, onto which the trajectory is projected along gravity to obtain corresponding terrain trajectory.
Figure 7:Effect of the input translation multiplier on NeoVerse.

Figure 8:Task-level performance across evaluation tracks.Two models per interface are compared across all eight tasks, ordered from static-scene diagnostics through Subject Control to World Reactivity; crosses mark unsupported tasks.

Figure 9:WorldExam Gallery.Representative test cases span first- and third-person viewpoints; human, animal, vehicle, and robot subjects; diverse indoor and outdoor scene content; and a range of terrain types.
